Fix: the Claude desktop app shows an "Allow Claude to start the session?" card on every mcp__ccd_session__start_session call, even in Bypass mode, because our guard hook lists that tool.

Proven cause (owner test, 2026-11-14 00:04 CST):
- The desktop app (Claude.app 5.11492.5) counts any PreToolUse hook whose matcher lists mcp__ccd_session__start_session as an "ask" rule. It does so even when the hook answers "allow". In app.asar .vite/build: createCanUseTool -> _e -> t.i$ (aDr) -> iDr returns true for any non-built-in PreToolUse hook whose matcher covers the tool. A regex-like matcher such as * counts too. A remote flag (3650263018) marks start_session "always_ask", which is what makes this check run.
- settings.json, hooks.PreToolUse entry 0 (the guard.py hook), lists mcp__ccd_session__start_session in its matcher. That alone causes the card on every start.
- Test: with start_session removed from every PreToolUse matcher, a fresh Bypass session started a session with no card. With it restored, the card came back.
- Public bug: anthropics/claude-code#103832 (open). permissions.allow and allow hooks don't help; they make it worse.

What the guard checks on start_session today (hooks/guard.py): SESSION_TOOL at line 2913. The model floor in floor_hit (~3072). The START_TOOLS checks (~4074): handoff-unread and related start rules. A load-brake skip (~4170). guard.log shows real denies on it: handoff-unread and agent-model-floor.

Pick and justify one: (a) the same checks fire on the session's next gated tool call (handoff-unread already does on Bash/Edit); (b) a PostToolUse audit on start_session that flags a bad start (wrong model, unread handoff) and tells the session to stop the new session; (c) drop the checks for start_session, with a debt record.
